translation_notes: context shim: infixowl_context.py is rdflib/extras/infixowl.py from the same commit, vendored verbatim except its dead `from rdflib import py3compat` import (replaced by a no-op stand-in); both sides import Class from it (Class is defined further down in the same module in the original)
`import logging` added to both sides: the extracted region uses logging.getLogger but the extractor did not carry the import
prefixes: OWL_NS->owl, RDF->rdf, RDFS->rdfs; the mechanical draft's `owl-ns` prefix is unusable outside islands (a hyphen stays subtraction in Python context)

OWL_NS = Namespace(...) is KEPT in the ldpy version, unlike the other infixowl regions: nsBinds stores the namespace itself as a value ('owl': OWL_NS), and @prefix declares no runtime object — so the owl namespace is written twice, once as a prefix (16 term references) and once as a Namespace (1 value). The mechanical draft dropped the assignment and left nsBinds referring to an undefined name.
URIRef('http://www.w3.org/2000/10/swap/list#') -> <...> island, valid in a dict-value position

the SPARQL query stays a Python string: its PREFIX prolog is *generated* from nsBinds by string formatting, so no island applies (islands do not reach inside strings) — this is exactly the case ldpy cannot improve
owl:maxCardinality/minCardinality/cardinality as dict *keys* transpile correctly (`{owl:maxCardinality: 'MAX'}`): the local part stops before the dict colon

driver: 10 fixtures cover the three boolean constructors, the restriction forms (allValuesFrom, someValuesFrom with a labelled property, maxCardinality), complementOf and the final fall-through (SPARQL probe + compute_qname, with and without a label); the owl:hasValue branch is left uncovered because it re-enters manchesterSyntax with a bytes term, which rdflib 7 rejects as a subject (a pre-existing Python-2 bug of the region, identical on both sides)
